articles.title: Korea’s SK Hynix shares make stellar US market debut, rocket 13% on continued AI optimism
articles.content: SK Hynix's U.S. shares surged thirteen percent on their Nasdaq debut. The South Korean chipmaker raised twenty-six point five billion dollars through a share sale. The company's listing provides funding for new factory construction.

articles.title: Fed officials fret over inflation risk, weigh rate hikes
articles.content: Federal Reserve officials remain concerned about persistent inflation pressures.  Incoming price reports will guide future interest rate decisions by policymakers. The central bank awaits crucial economic data to shape its next move.

articles.title: SK Hynix shares jump in marquee US debut as AI euphoria persists
articles.content: SK Hynix's Nasdaq debut saw its shares jump significantly after a large share sale.  This event signals strong investor enthusiasm for chip stocks amid the AI revolution. This listing aims to close valuation gaps and provide access to a larger investor pool.

articles.title: SBI Funds raises Rs 1,655 crore in a pre-IPO placement
articles.content: SBI Funds Management secured ₹1,655 crore from investors before its IPO.  This pre-IPO share sale occurred ahead of the company's upcoming public offering.  The asset manager's ₹11,693 crore IPO is the largest public issue scheduled for 2026.  PI Opportunities Fund-II and Enam's Akash Manek Bhanshali were among the significant investors.  The transaction involved selling a 1.42% stake at ₹574 per share.

articles.title: Groww faces technical glitch, client withdrawals hit
articles.content: Groww experienced a temporary disruption affecting client fund withdrawals on Friday.  This incident was attributed to an issue with its cloud service provider, Google Cloud Platform.  Some users also reported difficulties depositing money into their accounts.  The brokerage stated the problem was promptly resolved before market closing.  Customers could then access their funds after the disruption ended.

articles.title: IT rally powers markets over 1%; Sensex, Nifty end week with marginal losses
articles.content: Indian equity indices saw a rise on Friday, boosted by information technology stocks. Tata Consultancy Services' earnings met expectations, easing sector concerns which helped the market. The benchmark indices, however, finished the week marginally lower, ending a winning streak. Renewed West Asia tensions kept investor optimism in check earlier in the week. Brent crude futures traded above $76 a barrel on Friday evening.

articles.title: Forex reserves rise $7.3 billion as FCNR & ECB flows pick up
articles.content: The country's stockpile of assets denominated in foreign currencies rose $7.26 billion to $674 billion in the week ended July 3, the latest data from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) showed. Of the total reserves, foreign currency assets increased $4.5 billion to $545.5 billion, while gold reserves increased $2.6 billion to $105.2 billion during the week.

articles.title: Indian Bank drops capital raising plan on lower ECL hit
articles.content: Indian Bank has cancelled its planned share sale to raise funds. The lender's expected credit loss impact is now estimated lower than previously calculated. This revised calculation means the bank will not need to raise additional capital. The bank's net profit rose ten percent year-on-year in the fiscal first quarter. Gross advances and deposits also saw significant year-on-year growth.

articles.title: Bank credit growth at two-year high at 18.6% as debt market turns costlier
articles.content: Bank credit expanded significantly in the fortnight ending June 30. Deposit growth also showed a healthy increase during the same period. This credit demand stems from both consumer and corporate sectors. Corporate entities are increasingly favoring banks over debt markets for funding. The gap between credit and deposit growth widened to 570 basis points.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley warns AI chip rally may be running out of steam
articles.content: Morgan Stanley's Lisa Shalett warned semiconductor stocks may be overvalued as hyperscalers increasingly develop lower-cost proprietary AI chips. She expects slowing AI infrastructure spending and weaker pricing power to challenge chipmakers, despite continued investor interest and SK Hynix's Nasdaq debut.
